label: Aquinas, I q.7 a.2 co.: A created subsistent form has being contracted to its nature
interpretation: Aquinas distinguishes lack of material limitation, which can ground infinity in a respect, from absolute infinity. He argues that even in the immaterial case a created form has being without being its own act of being.
attribution: The passage states that even a created form that subsists apart from matter has received being contracted to a determinate nature and therefore is finite absolutely, which is the premise.
